result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick stacked cards, keep the desktop table for dispatchers, and add search, so they agree on the main approach. B orders the fields a little better for a rep on a call, putting items last and total/tracking higher, while A puts the items text above total and tracking. A wins on items 4 and 5: every value keeps its label on the card, the total is right-aligned with consistent decimals, and tracking has a Copy button. B's cards drop the labels ("Oct 9 · $84.20"), and A's implementation notes (a `<dl>`, `display: none`, screen-reader concerns) are more concrete. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend stacked cards with sticky search and keep the desktop table, so they are close. B does better on rubric item 4: Total and Tracking keep their labels, the total is right-aligned with the same decimals on every card, and the tracking number has a copy button that is easy to hit. B also gives an accessibility reason for its implementation. A's field order better matches what a rep needs on a call (items last, with a clear reason, and tracking links to the carrier), but A drops labels on the card and puts the total inline with the date.
